rules.summary: OCPS board policy says all district high schools are FHSAA members and follow FHSAA rules. The policy does not mention NIL.
rules.conditions: Policy JJI was adopted in 2008, before FHSAA allowed NIL. It adds no district NIL rule.
rules.citation: OCPS School Board Policy JJI, section (1)
rules.short_answer: The district policy points to FHSAA rules and says nothing on NIL.

sources.quote: All district high schools shall be members of the Florida High School --- Athletics Association, Inc. (FHSAA) and shall be governed by the rules and regulations adopted by FHSAA.

rules.summary: OCPS says athletes are under all school board rules and the Code of Student Conduct at athletic events and practices. OCPS also says the Board can withhold the privilege of taking part in extracurricular activities.
rules.conditions: These are general conduct rules. They are not written about NIL.
rules.citation: OCPS School Board Policy JJI (8) and Policy JJ
rules.short_answer: District conduct rules apply to athletes and can cost you the right to play.

sources.quote: All students shall be subject to all school board rules and to the Code of Student Conduct while attending athletic events and practices.
Pursuant to Florida law, the Board has the authority to withhold the privilege of participating in extracurricular activities from students.

rules.summary: OCPS says school board property cannot be used to advertise or promote a business unless there is a contract for advertising under Policy KHB.
rules.conditions: The policy is about advertising on district property in general. It does not mention student NIL deals. Display ads need a written Display Advertising Agreement arranged through the OCPS Marketing and Events Department.
rules.citation: OCPS School Board Policy KHB, sections (1) and (2)(c)
rules.short_answer: No business promotion on OCPS property without a district advertising contract.

sources.quote: shall not be used for advertising or otherwise promoting the interests of any commercial, religious, political, or other non-district agency or organization except by contractual agreement for “Advertising” as defined in this policy.
Such Display Advertising Agreement shall be provided through and assisted by the Marketing and Events Department.

rules.summary: OCPS says the principal or the Chief Facilities Officer may approve outside use of buildings, grounds or equipment through a facility use agreement. Business groups may be charged rent and must show insurance.
rules.conditions: The policy does not mention filming, photo shoots or NIL. The district Facilities page links facility rental to Facilitron.
rules.short_answer: Using a campus for an outside activity needs approval and a facility use agreement.

sources.quote: The use of Board Property shall not interfere with the educational program of the district or school.
may permit the use of Board Property by a civic, religious, business, or community organization for nonschool activities on a specific, temporary, or short-term basis.

rules.summary: OCPS says no advertisement on board property may promote alcohol, tobacco, drugs, weapons, gambling and similar content.
rules.conditions: This applies to advertising on OCPS property, websites and publications. It is not written as a rule for a student's own NIL deal.
rules.citation: OCPS School Board Policy KHB, section (6)(b)
rules.short_answer: Ads on OCPS property cannot promote alcohol, tobacco, drugs, weapons or gambling.

sources.quote: No advertisement shall promote or contain references to alcohol, tobacco, drugs, drug paraphernalia, weapons, or lewd, vulgar, obscene, pornographic or illegal materials or activities, gambling, violence, hatred, sexual conduct or sexually explicit material

rules.summary: The OCPS Style Guide page sets rules for the district logo in district communications. It does not state a rule for students or outside businesses using district or school logos.
rules.conditions: No School Board policy on school names, logos or trademarks was found in the policy index. Policy KHB only speaks about product brand names and logos.
rules.citation: OCPS Style Guide Home, Logos section
rules.short_answer: No public district rule on using school logos in NIL content was found.

sources.quote: The logo is mandatory on all external communication pieces created and distributed by the district.
Brand names, trademarks, logos, or tags for product or service identification purposes are not considered advertising.

school_policy.summary: The Winter Park athletics site has a menu item named NIL under 'More'. It opens a hosted copy of the FHSAA GA1 Affidavit of Amateurism dated August 2024. The site gives no school-written NIL guidance beside it.

rules.summary: Winter Park's athletics site has a menu item called NIL. It opens a copy of FHSAA Form GA1 (Affidavit of Amateurism). The site adds no NIL rules of its own.
rules.conditions: School-specific part: the school posts the form under an NIL label. The copy is the August 2024 version and may not be the current FHSAA form.
rules.short_answer: The school's NIL link is the FHSAA GA1 form, with no extra school guidance.

rules.summary: Winter Park's eligibility page says an athlete must be an amateur and must not accept money, gifts or donations for participating in a sport.
rules.conditions: This restates FHSAA Bylaw 9.9 on an undated school page. It does not mention NIL and may pre-date the 2024 FHSAA NIL change.
rules.citation: Winter Park FHSAA Eligibility And Compliance page, item 9
rules.short_answer: The school page says no money or gifts for playing a sport.

sources.quote: Must be an amateur. This means you must not accept money, gifts, or donations for participating in a sport. (FHSAA Bylaw 9.9)

contacts.office: Winter Park High School Athletic Training Program
contacts.role: Director of Athletic Training Services, handles online physical and clearance submissions

disclosure_workflow.what: Yearly online clearance (EL2 physical, OCPS Cardiology Report, NFHS certificates) on Home Campus. Separately, the site posts Form GA1 under an 'NIL' menu item. The pages do not say how or when GA1 must be turned in.
disclosure_workflow.recipient: Winter Park High School Athletic Training Program through Home Campus
disclosure_workflow.deadline_text: It takes up to 2 school days to process paperwork, sometimes longer at the beginning of the season. Same day clearance is not possible.
disclosure_workflow.form_name: GA1 Affidavit of Amateurism (posted under the NIL menu item)
disclosure_workflow.quote: 1. Go to https://www.homecampus.com/login o New site so everyone must make a new account.

important_claims: The athletics site has a menu item labelled 'NIL' that links to GA1_Affidavit_of_Amateurism_81624-1.pdf.
The eligibility page says athletes must not accept money, gifts or donations for participating in a sport, citing FHSAA Bylaw 9.9.
2026-27 clearance is on Home Campus, described as a new site where everyone must make a new account.
Athletic Director is Charles Battaglini, as printed on the Winter Park Head Coaches page.
Winter Park appears on the FHSAA Membership List 2026-27.
ambiguities: The GA1 copy is the 8/16/24 version. FHSAA may have revised the form since, so the school copy could be outdated.
The eligibility page is undated and its amateur wording does not mention the NIL exception. It should not be shown as the school's full position on NIL.
The pages do not say whether GA1 is collected through Home Campus or handed in another way.
winterparkhs.ocps.net/athletics-home returns a 404 page, so the school site profile could not be cross-checked there.
Sports list is taken from the team menu data on the official athletics site. It may include inactive or non-FHSAA teams and should be checked.
manual_review: https://sportshub2-uploads.vnn-prod.zone/files/sites/68/2024/08/22190831/GA1_Affidavit_of_Amateurism_81624-1.pdf : open to confirm the form version and whether the school added any cover text
https://www.homecampus.com/login : log-in portal, check whether GA1 is a signature step
